expectations.text: A spec for the overdue feature exists under OUTPUT_DIR/repo/docs/product-specs/, either as a new file with a new prefix or as new criteria appended to tickets.md or cli.md with fresh IDs; the transcript or spec says which was chosen and why.
expectations.evidence: Re-judged on a second pass, which found a miss. The transcript's Decisions section reads: 'Create against amend: a new feature file overdue.md with prefix OVD ... The command surface is amended in cli.md, which mirrors how tickets.md (TKT-013) and cli.md (CLI-006) split listing today.' A thin reason, but a reason.

expectations.text: The spec has a one-paragraph intro, a `Prefix:` line, and a Non-goals section with at least two non-goals that are real boundaries (for example no notifications, no SLA pause on weekends, no change to the event log format).
expectations.evidence: Intro paragraph: 'Support agents see which tickets have passed their due time and still need work. `ticketdesk list` marks each such ticket `OVERDUE`. The new command `ticketdesk overdue` lists only those tickets...'. 'Prefix: `OVD`.' present. '## Non-goals' with 8 bolded boundaries (no fourth state, no overdue event, no notifications, no due-time change, no breach history, no filters, no due time/lateness in output, no other evaluation time). Also '## Goals'.

expectations.text: At least five criteria headed `### PREFIX-NNN: Title` with zero-padded three-digit numbers (a letter suffix such as TKT-014A is allowed), unique within the file; no `**Testable:**` lines. Body length is judged separately: most bodies are one to three sentences, and a longer body is noted, not a failure.
expectations.evidence: 10 new criteria: OVD-001..OVD-008 (check_run items=8, all new) plus CLI-010, CLI-011. Correct headings, unique, no Testable lines. Bodies 2-4 sentences; OVD-007 (4 sentences) is a scenario.

expectations.text: Criteria cover: the OVERDUE marker in `list` output; the `overdue` command's filter; the oldest-due-first order; a ticket exactly at its due time; closed tickets (either excluded, or an open question); and what the user sees when nothing is overdue (output and exit code).
expectations.evidence: Marker: CLI-010 '#<id> [<priority>] <state> OVERDUE <title>' and OVD-003 'marks every overdue ticket and no other ticket'. Filter: OVD-004 'shows every overdue ticket once and no other ticket'. Order: OVD-004 'due time, earliest first... ID order, lowest first'. Exact due: OVD-001 'At exactly its due time, a ticket is not yet overdue.' Closed: OVD-002 'not overdue... closed before... and... after it'. Empty: CLI-011 'With no overdue tickets it prints nothing and exits with code 0.' OVD-005 'shows no tickets and succeeds' also covers it. Stated as criteria, not flagged as an assumption.

expectations.text: Every criterion body is behavioral: no function, class, module, or file names (such as TicketService, due_at, cli.py); outcomes are described as what the user sees in the CLI output or exit code.
expectations.evidence: No implementation names in new bodies (impl_words=0). OVD-008 states the corrupt-log outcome in terms of output and exit code.

expectations.text: The spec respects INV-001 and INV-002: overdue is a derived state computed from the ticket's due time and is not written to the event log; if the spec proposes a new event kind, it flags that as a change to LOG-002 and the invariants needing sign-off.
expectations.evidence: Intro: 'Overdue is not a ticket state. The help desk computes it from the due time and the time at which a command runs. The event log never records it.' Non-goals: 'No overdue event.' OVD-006: 'No event is appended when a ticket becomes overdue.' INV-001/INV-002 not cited by ID (questions.md Q3 cites TKT-001 and LOG-009).

expectations.text: The spec does not contradict TKT-005 (due time by priority) or TKT-013 (listing order of `list`): it reuses the existing due time and states how OVERDUE interacts with the existing list order rather than redefining it.
expectations.evidence: Intro: 'The due time of a ticket comes from TKT-005.' OVD-003 states outright: 'The list still contains every ticket in the order of TKT-013. Every line still shows the state of its ticket.' Amended CLI-006 keeps 'in ID order, see TKT-013'.

expectations.text: docs/product-specs/README.md is updated: the new file appears in the prefix table and the index with a one-line summary (or, if criteria were appended to an existing file, the README needed no change and the spec says so).
expectations.evidence: README prefix table gains the `OVD` row; index gains 'Overdue tickets: when a ticket is overdue, the mark in the list, the `overdue` command and its order. Draft, awaiting sign-off.' AGENTS.md gains an OVD row.

expectations.text: Open questions are listed at the end of the spec (or in OUTPUT_DIR/questions.md) and assumptions are marked inline; none of them is silently resolved in a criterion.
expectations.evidence: '## Open questions' at the end of overdue.md (Q-1..Q-4, each with the draft's assumption and a criterion ID) plus questions.md (3 shape + 5). The non-goal 'No due time or lateness in the output' points inline to Q-3. The boundary and tie-order assumptions are only in questions.md (Q4, Q6), not in the in-file list.

expectations.text: Skim test: the intro paragraph's first sentence says what the feature is for a support agent; each criterion title names the behavior; no lead is a teaser or a qualifier chain.
expectations.evidence: First sentence of the feature intro: 'Support agents see which tickets have passed their due time and still need work.' It says what the feature does for its user. The Status line follows the intro paragraph. Titles name behaviors ('When a ticket is overdue', 'Overdue in the ticket list', 'Overdue follows the clock', 'A corrupt log stops the overdue list'); 'CLI-011: overdue' is a bare command name.
